title: Hypergroup Symmetry in Relative Quantum Field Theories and Chiral Algebras
summary:
A QFT is said to be relative if it lives at the boundary of a topological QFT in one higher dimension. We develop a general framework for working with noninvertible symmetries of relative theories in two spacetime dimensions, extending several well-known results for absolute QFTs. We emphasize various new features which arise in the relative setting, including the role of topological surfaces of the bulk, and the appearance of hypergroups and certain generalizations of tube algebras known as dome algebras. Our formalism is particularly well-suited for studying rational chiral algebras, where it predicts that finite symmetries are in explicit one-to-one correspondence with conformal embeddings of finite index.
  We describe several implications of our framework for absolute theories. First, we explain how to "glue" together symmetries of the left- and right-moving chiral algebras of a 2D CFT to produce topological line defects of the full theory. Second, we derive a precise correspondence between boundary conditions of a 2D CFT and symmetries of its chiral algebra. This correspondence has several structural corollaries: in diagonal rational CFTs, we demonstrate that the topological line defects of the theory act transitively on its boundary conditions, and further that the identity Cardy state has the smallest $g$-function amongst all boundary conditions, including those which only preserve Virasoro symmetry.
  We conclude by illustrating our results in a variety of examples. For instance, we show that, if there exists a rational chiral algebra with central charge $c=8$ whose modular tensor category is the Drinfeld center of the Haagerup fusion category, then it must arise as the fixed points of a rank-2 hypergroup acting on the $SU(3)_1\otimes (E_{6})_1$ chiral algebra.

AI.tldr: A framework for noninvertible symmetries of relative QFTs in 2D is developed, linking to bulk topological QFTs, hypergroups, and dome algebras; applied to rational chiral algebras, 2D CFT boundary conditions, and specific examples like Haagerup fusion categories.
AI.motivation: To extend known results about noninvertible symmetries from absolute QFTs to relative QFTs (theories living at the boundary of a topological QFT in one higher dimension), addressing new features such as bulk topological surfaces, hypergroups, and dome algebras.
AI.method: Develops a general formalism for noninvertible symmetries in relative 2D theories, leveraging the bulk-boundary correspondence in TQFTs, introducing hypergroups and dome algebras, and applying the framework to rational chiral algebras and 2D CFTs.
AI.result: Finite symmetries of rational chiral algebras correspond to conformal embeddings of finite index. Topological line defects of a full 2D CFT are obtained by gluing left/right chiral algebra symmetries. Boundary conditions of a 2D CFT correspond to symmetries of its chiral algebra. In diagonal RCFTs, topological lines act transitively on boundary conditions, and the identity Cardy state has the smallest g-function.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a unified understanding of noninvertible symmetries in relative 2D QFTs, with concrete predictions such as the Haagerup fusion category realization via a rank-2 hypergroup acting on SU(3)₁ ⊗ (E₆)₁ chiral algebra.

title: Kaleidoscopes, Waves and the Prepotential
summary: Isomorphic flops are topology-changing transitions connecting two diffeomorphic families of Calabi-Yau threefolds. They correspond to the generators of certain Coxeter groups acting on the moduli space. As a consequence of these symmetries, the prepotential of 4D $\mathcal{N} = 2$ Type IIA compactifications on such varieties must assemble into Coxeter-invariant functions. We construct a database of all Coxeter symmetries from isomorphic flops in Kähler-favorable CICYs. The action of the Coxeter group on the Kähler moduli space leaves a symmetric bilinear form invariant, which we interpret as a metric and construct its associated Laplace-Beltrami operator. We argue that the Coxeter-invariant functions featured in the prepotential solve the Helmholtz equation with this Laplacian, and that the prepotential can then be resummed into a decomposition in terms of eigenfunctions of the Laplace-Beltrami operator. The convergence rate of the raw orbit sums of worldsheet instanton contributions and the resummed expressions are complementary, with the latter sharply localizing around the first few terms in the interior of the moduli space.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that Coxeter symmetries from isomorphic flops in Calabi-Yau threefolds impose invariant structures on the prepotential of 4D N=2 Type IIA compactifications. The authors construct a database of such symmetries, interpret the invariant bilinear form as a metric, and show the prepotential solves the Helmholtz equation, enabling a resummation into eigenfunctions that converge faster than raw orbit sums.
AI.motivation: To understand how isomorphic flops (topology-changing transitions between diffeomorphic families of Calabi-Yau threefolds) generate Coxeter symmetries that constrain the prepotential in 4D N=2 Type IIA string compactifications, and to develop efficient resummation techniques for worldsheet instanton contributions.
AI.method: Construct a database of all Coxeter symmetries from isomorphic flops in Kähler-favorable CICYs. The Coxeter group acts on the Kähler moduli space, leaving a symmetric bilinear form invariant which is interpreted as a metric. The associated Laplace-Beltrami operator is constructed, and the prepotential is shown to satisfy the Helmholtz equation. The prepotential is then decomposed into eigenfunctions of this operator.
AI.result: Coxeter-invariant functions in the prepotential solve the Helmholtz equation with the Laplace-Beltrami operator derived from the invariant bilinear form. The resummed expressions localize sharply around the first few terms in the interior of the moduli space, offering complementary convergence properties to raw orbit sums of worldsheet instanton contributions.
AI.conclusion: The Coxeter symmetry framework provides a systematic way to organize and resum the prepotential, with the resummed form converging faster and localizing in the moduli space interior, complementing the raw orbit sum approach.

title: The Double Well Done Doubly-Well
summary: The symmetric double-well potential is one of the simplest quantum-mechanical systems in which perturbative and non-perturbative physics are deeply entangled. Its energy levels have non-analytic expansions in inverse powers of the inter-well separation, with factorially growing coefficients, while the parity splitting is exponentially small and invisible to perturbation theory. Resurgence ties the two features together, organizing the exact spectrum into a single tightly-constrained trans-series. This paper gives a self-contained account of this trans-series from two complementary approaches: exact WKB and the Euclidean path integral, developed in a common notation with explicit calculations through the four-instanton level and three-loop order. In exact WKB, Stokes phenomena encoded in the Delabaere--Dillinger--Pham relations control the analytic continuation of the wavefunction past turning points. The quantization condition expressed in terms of Voros symbols then determines the full trans-series. The DDP relations are local and do not require knowing the global topology of the energy surface, but that surface is an elliptic curve. In the path integral, elliptic curves enter differently: the classical saddle points are doubly-periodic elliptic functions of Euclidean time, and Stokes phenomena play out within the finite-dimensional manifold of quasi-zero modes rather than through analytic continuation of the wavefunction. A Lefschetz thimble decomposition determines which saddles contribute, and the resulting partition function trans-series is much simpler than the energy trans-series: at each instanton order the $T$-dependence is a polynomial fixed by the quasi-zero-mode thimble integrals. Together, the two approaches deploy a shared mathematical infrastructure in complementary ways, showing that the double well is an ideal setting to explore resurgence.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a self-contained study of the symmetric double-well potential using resurgence theory, developing trans-series for energy levels via two complementary approaches (exact WKB and Euclidean path integral) with explicit calculations through four-instanton level and three-loop order.
AI.motivation: To understand how perturbative and non-perturbative physics are entangled in the double-well potential — a simple system where energy levels have non-analytic expansions with factorially growing coefficients and exponentially small parity splitting invisible to perturbation theory — and to show that resurgence ties these features together into a unified trans-series.
AI.method: Two complementary approaches are developed in a common notation: (1) exact WKB, where Delabaere-Dillinger-Pham (DDP) relations control Stokes phenomena for analytic continuation of the wavefunction, with quantization condition expressed via Voros symbols; (2) Euclidean path integral, where classical saddles are doubly-periodic elliptic functions, Stokes phenomena occur in quasi-zero-mode manifolds, and Lefschetz thimble decomposition determines saddle contributions.
AI.result: Explicit trans-series calculations through four-instanton level and three-loop order. The path integral partition function trans-series is significantly simpler than the energy trans-series — at each instanton order, the T-dependence is a polynomial fixed by quasi-zero-mode thimble integrals.
AI.conclusion: The two approaches deploy shared mathematical infrastructure (elliptic curves, resurgence) in complementary ways, demonstrating that the double well is an ideal system for exploring resurgence theory.

title: String dualities and wedge singularities
summary: We study strings propagating in backgrounds with a wedge singularity, namely whose internal sector describes a wedge sum of closed manifolds. We focus on the wedge sum of two circles, which was recently argued to provide a quantum geometry for an M-theoretic description of type 0 strings, along with a much wider non-supersymmetric duality web stemming from quotients thereof. In the context of this proposal, we investigate whether the worldsheet features of type IIA strings, together with strong-coupling ingredients, can consistently reproduce the expectation of a weakly coupled type 0A frame. To this end, we combine worldsheet effects due to the wedge singularity with the emergence proposal applied to D0-branes probing it. We find that the resulting potential reproduces the correct tree-level mass of the tachyon in a specific scaling limit. We also discuss the possibility of kinematic obstructions to our worldsheet approach using the framework of topological modular forms, and comment on some puzzles and open questions.

AI.tldr: The paper studies string propagation on backgrounds with a wedge singularity, specifically the wedge sum of two circles, which is proposed to provide a quantum geometry for M-theoretic descriptions of type 0 strings. By combining worldsheet effects from the wedge singularity with the emergence proposal applied to D0-branes, the authors find that the resulting potential reproduces the correct tree-level tachyon mass in a specific scaling limit. They also discuss kinematic obstructions using topological modular forms.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether worldsheet features of type IIA strings, combined with strong-coupling ingredients, can consistently reproduce the expectation of a weakly coupled type 0A frame, in the context of a proposal that wedge sums of circles provide a quantum geometry for M-theoretic descriptions of type 0 strings and a non-supersymmetric duality web.
AI.method: Combining worldsheet effects due to the wedge singularity with the emergence proposal applied to D0-branes probing it; utilizing topological modular forms to discuss kinematic obstructions.
AI.result: The resulting potential reproduces the correct tree-level mass of the tachyon in a specific scaling limit.
AI.conclusion: The approach successfully reproduces the tree-level tachyon mass, but there remain puzzles and open questions, including potential kinematic obstructions from topological modular forms.

title: Big Axions
summary: We introduce big axions: axion models in which a Nambu-Goldstone mode emerges from the collective spontaneous breaking of a network of U(1) symmetries delocalized in theory space. Big axions naturally realize high-quality accidental global symmetries, admit both pre- and post-inflationary cosmological histories, and exhibit rich topological structures that interpolate between ordinary Peccei-Quinn axions and axions which descend from extra-dimensional gauge fields. We identify a minimal phenomenologically viable subclass, little big axions, and demonstrate that they provide a robust solution to the strong charge-parity problem in quantum chromodynamics while potentially accounting for some or all of the dark matter of the universe.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces "big axions"—axion models where a Nambu-Goldstone mode arises from collective spontaneous breaking of multiple U(1) symmetries delocalized in theory space. These models realize high-quality accidental symmetries, support pre- and post-inflationary cosmologies, and interpolate between standard Peccei-Quinn axions and extra-dimensional gauge field axions. The subclass "little big axions" offers a robust solution to the strong CP problem and can account for some or all dark matter.
AI.motivation: To overcome limitations of ordinary axion models (e.g., quality/fine-tuning issues) by constructing novel axion models with collective symmetry breaking in theory space, enabling high-quality accidental global symmetries and richer topological structures.
AI.method: The authors propose a framework where the axion emerges from collective spontaneous breaking of a network of U(1) symmetries delocalized across multiple sites in theory space. They analyze the resulting topological structures, symmetry quality, and phenomenological viability, and identify a minimal viable subclass termed "little big axions."
AI.result: Big axions provide high-quality accidental global symmetries, support both pre- and post-inflationary cosmologies, and exhibit a topological spectrum bridging standard QCD axions and extra-dimensional axions. Little big axions are identified as a minimal viable subclass that robustly solves the strong CP problem and can constitute dark matter.
AI.conclusion: Big axion models offer a new, flexible framework for axion physics that resolves quality issues, enriches cosmological and topological possibilities, and remains phenomenologically viable through the little big axion subclass.

title: Unitarity, Recursion and Soft Limits in (EA)dS through Dressing
summary: Using the recently developed framework in which cosmological correlators in (E)AdS are represented as flat-space amplitudes dressed by auxiliary propagators, we show that several structural properties of the cosmological observables have a direct flat-space origin. We derive cosmological cutting rules for spinning correlators from the flat-space optical theorem, obtain the cosmological tree theorem from the Feynman tree theorem, and uplift BCFW recursion relations to (E)AdS via dressing. We also show that flat-space soft theorems reproduce the soft limits of (E)AdS correlators, and find indications of an emergent universal structure in subleading soft limits. These results provide evidence that key features of cosmological correlators can be systematically understood as dressed manifestations of flat-space physics.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that cosmological correlators in (E)AdS can be understood as dressed flat-space amplitudes, deriving cutting rules, tree theorem, BCFW recursion, and soft theorems from flat-space physics.
AI.motivation: To establish a systematic framework connecting cosmological correlators in (E)AdS to flat-space amplitudes, revealing that structural properties of cosmological observables have direct flat-space origins.
AI.method: Using the recently developed framework where cosmological correlators in (E)AdS are represented as flat-space amplitudes dressed by auxiliary propagators; then deriving cosmological analogs of flat-space theorems including cutting rules, tree theorem, BCFW recursion, and soft theorems.
AI.result: Cosmological cutting rules for spinning correlators derived from flat-space optical theorem; cosmological tree theorem obtained from Feynman tree theorem; BCFW recursion relations uplifted to (E)AdS; flat-space soft theorems reproduce soft limits of (E)AdS correlators; evidence of emergent universal structure in subleading soft limits.
AI.conclusion: Key features of cosmological correlators can be systematically understood as dressed manifestations of flat-space physics.

title: The Future of Lepton Flavor
summary: The flavor puzzle remains one of the biggest open questions in particle theory to date and upcoming results from neutrino experiments will have a large impact on its potential solution in the future. While some classes of leptonic flavor models are difficult to constrain with current data, this will change in the coming years as several yet unknown quantities, like the neutrino mass ordering and the octant of $θ_{23}$, will be determined, and the CP-violating quantity $δ$ will be measured with some precision. In addition, significant improvements in the precision of the other oscillation parameters, notably $θ_{12}$, is also expected to impact our understanding of flavor. Together with anticipated improvements on the absolute neutrino mass scale determination from the combination of cosmological data sets or beta decay endpoint spectrum measurements, upcoming experiments will lead to a refined picture of our understanding of flavor in the lepton sector. In this paper, we show exactly how flavor model predictions relate to expected measurements. Five popular classes of leptonic flavor model predictions are considered: mass sum rules, one and two texture-zeros for both Dirac and Majorana neutrinos, charged lepton corrections, modular symmetries, and constrained sequential dominance. We discuss correlations, degeneracies, and discrimination capabilities in the context of the expected measurements from upcoming experiments. We also highlight how different flavor model predictions can be differentiated and the roles each upcoming observable has on flavor model predictions. We anticipate that the precision targeted in future measurements will be sufficient to dramatically reduce the number of viable leptonic flavor models, will allow us to disentangle them, and could hopefully begin to shed light on the answer to the flavor puzzle.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes how upcoming neutrino experiments will constrain and discriminate among five popular classes of leptonic flavor models (mass sum rules, texture zeros, charged lepton corrections, modular symmetries, constrained sequential dominance), showing that improved measurements of oscillation parameters, CP violation, mass ordering, and absolute neutrino mass scale will dramatically reduce the number of viable models and help solve the flavor puzzle.
AI.motivation: The flavor puzzle—understanding the pattern of fermion masses and mixing—remains a major open question in particle physics; upcoming neutrino experiments will provide crucial data to constrain theoretical flavor models.
AI.method: The authors consider five popular classes of leptonic flavor model predictions (mass sum rules, one and two texture-zeros for Dirac and Majorana neutrinos, charged lepton corrections, modular symmetries, constrained sequential dominance) and analyze how expected future measurements (neutrino mass ordering, θ23 octant, δ CP phase, improved θ12 precision, absolute mass scale from cosmology/beta decay) correlate with, degenerate among, and discriminate between these model predictions.
AI.result: Future measurements with improved precision will be sufficient to dramatically reduce the number of viable leptonic flavor models and enable disentanglement between different model classes, with correlations and degeneracies identified for each observable.
AI.conclusion: Upcoming experimental data will significantly constrain leptonic flavor models, allowing discrimination among them and potentially shedding light on the flavor puzzle.

title: Krylov Complexity: Flat bands and Carroll breaking deformations
summary: Systems with flat band structures, when written in the language of Compact Localised States (CLS), have been shown to be explicitly invariant under supertranslation symmetries, making Carrollian symmetries inherently important for such systems. In this work, we explore the state dynamics of these systems, focusing on quenches induced by Carroll breaking perturbations, through the probe of Krylov (spread) Complexity. We specialise to Fermionic ladder Hamiltonians with all bands flat (ABF) scenario, augmented by a supertranslation preserving interaction, and discuss Krylov state complexity for quenches across critical lines. We further discuss how the growth of Krylov complexity sharply resolves the phase-dependent resilience of Carrollian sectors against delocalising perturbations. This is augmented by a complementary mechanism for Krylov growth in a continuum Carroll scalar field theory with a gradient deformation, which exhibits strong ultraviolet sensitivity (UV/IR mixing).

AI.tldr: The paper explores Krylov (spread) complexity in flat band systems with Carrollian symmetries, focusing on quenches from Carroll-breaking perturbations in fermionic ladder Hamiltonians and a continuum Carroll scalar field theory with UV/IR mixing.
AI.motivation: Flat band systems exhibit Carrollian (supertranslation) symmetries, and the authors aim to understand state dynamics under symmetry-breaking perturbations using Krylov complexity as a probe.
AI.method: The authors study Krylov state complexity in (i) all-bands-flat (ABF) fermionic ladder Hamiltonians with supertranslation-preserving interactions, analyzing quenches across critical lines, and (ii) a continuum Carroll scalar field theory with a gradient deformation.
AI.result: Krylov complexity growth sharply resolves phase-dependent resilience of Carrollian sectors against delocalising perturbations; the scalar field example exhibits strong UV/IR mixing.
AI.conclusion: Krylov complexity is an effective diagnostic for probing Carrollian symmetry breaking and delocalization transitions in flat band systems, with implications for both lattice and continuum settings.

title: Heavy-element paleodetectors for Higgsino dark matter
summary: Paleodetectors have been proposed as a new approach to direct detection of weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs), through the search for damage tracks in ancient minerals induced by WIMP-nucleon scattering. However, for inelastic dark matter such as the Higgsino, existing paleodetector targets lack sufficiently heavy nuclei to overcome the kinematic threshold for scattering. We propose heavy-element paleodetectors as a new probe of inelastic dark matter, using ancient, radiopure minerals containing heavy elements such as lead. We identify brine precipitates from deep geothermal aquifers as a possible geological source of such minerals. Additionally, paleodetectors are uniquely sensitive to the history of the dark matter high-velocity tail, including a possible fast population induced by the Large Magellanic Cloud's close approach 50 Myr ago. Such a scenario would favor younger minerals than usually assumed in the paleodetector literature. This method can probe Higgsino mass splittings up to $δ\simeq 920$ keV. Due to the large Higgsino-nucleon cross section, we find that even suboptimal mineral samples with ordinary radioactivity from depths of only 2 km can probe new parameter space, thus partially relaxing the stringent requirements on radiopurity and depth that constitute two significant challenges for the paleodetector program.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes heavy-element paleodetectors (using ancient minerals containing lead from brine precipitates) to detect inelastic dark matter like Higgsinos, which previously had kinematic thresholds too high for standard paleodetectors. It also highlights paleodetectors' sensitivity to the dark matter velocity tail history and the Large Magellanic Cloud's past flyby, showing that even suboptimal samples at moderate depths can probe new parameter space due to large Higgsino-nucleon cross sections.
AI.motivation: Standard paleodetector targets lack sufficiently heavy nuclei to overcome the kinematic threshold for inelastic dark matter scattering (e.g., Higgsino), motivating the need for heavy-element paleodetectors to probe this parameter space.
AI.method: The authors propose using ancient, radiopure minerals containing heavy elements such as lead, specifically brine precipitates from deep geothermal aquifers. They also consider the impact of the Large Magellanic Cloud's close approach 50 Myr ago on the dark matter velocity tail and the corresponding optimal mineral age.
AI.result: This method can probe Higgsino mass splittings up to δ ≃ 920 keV. Even suboptimal mineral samples with ordinary radioactivity from depths of only 2 km can probe new parameter space, relaxing requirements on radiopurity and depth.
AI.conclusion: Heavy-element paleodetectors offer a viable new probe of inelastic dark matter, with relaxed constraints on radiopurity and depth compared to traditional paleodetector requirements.

title: Mass-Flow Invariance of $Q$-Cohomology in BMN Matrix Quantum Mechanics
summary: We study the dependence of the dynamical supercharges of BMN matrix quantum mechanics on the mass parameter $μ$. Taking the $μ$-derivative at fixed canonical matrix variables, we show that the sixteen-component supercharge evolves by the adjoint action of a Hermitian quadratic bosonic operator $\mathcal{K}$, together with the spinor-space factor $iγ^{123}$. After projection to a $γ^{123}$-eigenspace, this flow integrates to a finite similarity transformation. For the nilpotent component $Q(μ)=\mathcal Q^4_-(μ)$, one obtains $Q(μ)=M(μ,μ_0)Q(μ_0)M(μ,μ_0)^{-1}$, giving an algebraic mass-flow non-renormalization statement for the $Q$-cohomology. The corresponding Hilbert-space statement has an analytic qualification, parallel to Witten's argument for supersymmetric quantum mechanics: $M$ is non-unitary and unbounded, so its action on the normalizable domain must be controlled. We formulate a small-step criterion by comparing the quadratic growth of $M$ with the Gaussian falloff of BMN oscillator wavefunctions within each component $μ>0$ or $μ<0$. As a concrete check, we evaluate this condition in the $N=2$ theory, whose two vacuum sectors are built on the trivial vacuum and the irreducible fuzzy-sphere vacuum. We also compute the induced $Q_{\rm BPS}$-action on the corresponding BPS letters: in the trivial sector it agrees with the standard BMN-sector BPS-letter differential of $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, while in the irreducible sector it vanishes.

AI.tldr: The paper studies how dynamical supercharges in BMN matrix quantum mechanics depend on the mass parameter μ, showing they evolve via a similarity transformation generated by a Hermitian quadratic bosonic operator. This yields a non-renormalization result for Q-cohomology, with analytic control via a small-step criterion comparing Gaussian falloff and quadratic growth. The N=2 case is checked, showing BPS-letter differential matching N=4 SYM in the trivial sector and vanishing in the irreducible sector.
AI.motivation: To understand the μ-dependence of supercharges in BMN matrix quantum mechanics and prove non-renormalization of Q-cohomology under mass flow, with analytic control analogous to Witten's argument for supersymmetric quantum mechanics.
AI.method: Taking μ-derivative at fixed canonical variables to show supercharge evolves via adjoint action of a Hermitian quadratic bosonic operator K with spinor factor iγ^{123}. Projecting to γ^{123}-eigenspace integrates to a finite similarity transformation. A small-step criterion compares quadratic growth of M with Gaussian falloff of BMN wavefunctions. Checked explicitly in N=2 theory with two vacuum sectors.
AI.result: The nilpotent component Q(μ) satisfies Q(μ)=M(μ,μ₀)Q(μ₀)M(μ,μ₀)^{-1}, giving algebraic mass-flow non-renormalization. The small-step criterion controls the unbounded non-unitary transformation. In N=2, the BPS-letter differential in the trivial sector matches N=4 SYM, while it vanishes in the irreducible fuzzy-sphere vacuum sector.
AI.conclusion: The mass-flow non-renormalization holds for Q-cohomology with analytic qualifications; the N=2 check confirms the framework's validity and reveals sector-dependent behavior of BPS letters.

title: NNLO+PS Higgs-pair production in MiNNLOPS
summary: We consider Higgs-boson pair production in gluon fusion at hadron colliders and match next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) QCD corrections to parton showers within the MiNNLO$_{PS}$ framework. Since the full top-quark mass dependence at this order is not available, finite top-quark mass effects are incorporated through approximations based on the exact NLO QCD result, using the available two-loop amplitude in the full theory. Specifically, the Born, single-virtual, single-real and double-real contributions are included exactly, while the real--virtual and double-virtual corrections are approximated. We consider different approximations for the latter to assess the associated uncertainties. We validate our predictions against fixed-order NNLO QCD results and compare with existing NNLO calculations matched to parton shower from GENEVA, where in some cases we find noticeable differences. Finally, we present phenomenological results for different Higgs-decay channels and variations of the trilinear Higgs coupling. Our MiNNLO$_{PS}$ generator for Higgs-boson pair production is available within the POWHEG-BOX-RES framework.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the matching of NNLO QCD corrections to parton showers for Higgs-boson pair production in gluon fusion using the MiNNLOPS framework, incorporating finite top-quark mass effects via approximations based on exact NLO QCD results, and providing phenomenological results for different Higgs-decay channels and variations of the trilinear Higgs coupling.
AI.motivation: To improve the theoretical precision for Higgs-boson pair production at hadron colliders by matching NNLO QCD corrections to parton showers, while incorporating finite top-quark mass effects since the full top-quark mass dependence at NNLO is not available.
AI.method: The MiNNLOPS framework is used to match NNLO QCD corrections to parton showers. Finite top-quark mass effects are included through approximations based on the exact NLO QCD result: Born, single-virtual, single-real, and double-real contributions are included exactly, while real-virtual and double-virtual corrections are approximated. Different approximations for the latter are considered to assess uncertainties.
AI.result: The predictions are validated against fixed-order NNLO QCD results and compared with existing NNLO+PS calculations from GENEVA, with noticeable differences observed in some cases. The generator is made available within the POWHEG-BOX-RES framework.
AI.conclusion: The MiNNLOPS generator for Higgs-boson pair production, incorporating finite top-quark mass effects through well-defined approximations, is now available and provides improved phenomenological predictions for different Higgs-decay channels and variations of the trilinear Higgs coupling.

title: Non-linear evolution of five-dimensional black strings in effective field theory
summary: We use numerical relativity to study the non-linear instability of five-dimensional black strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity. Black strings evolve into a series of black holes joined by thinner string-like segments, but key features of the dynamics depend on the sign of the Gauss-Bonnet coupling. For positive coupling, favored by UV considerations, the growth of curvature invariants is limited within the validity of effective field theory (EFT), suggesting a mechanism for restoring weak cosmic censorship. For negative coupling this cap is absent and curvatures may grow until the EFT breaks down.

AI.tldr: Numerical relativity study of 5D black string instability in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity, showing that positive GB coupling caps curvature growth within EFT validity (suggesting weak cosmic censorship restoration), while negative coupling allows unbounded curvature growth and EFT breakdown.
AI.motivation: To understand the non-linear instability of five-dimensional black strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity and how the sign of the Gauss-Bonnet coupling affects curvature growth and effective field theory validity.
AI.method: Numerical relativity simulations of black string evolution in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity in five dimensions.
AI.result: For positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling, curvature invariant growth is capped within EFT validity; for negative coupling, curvatures grow unboundedly until EFT breaks down.
AI.conclusion: Positive GB coupling may restore weak cosmic censorship via curvature cap within EFT, while negative coupling leads to EFT breakdown.

title: Interference effects in gluon-fusion Higgs boson production
comment: 13 pages, 2 tables, 2 figures, contribution to the LHC Higgs Working Group Report 5
summary: In this contribution we summarize recent progress in higher-order computations of signal-background interference effects in Higgs boson production via gluon fusion. The focus is on the resonance region, where interference terms are most significant relative to the pure signal contribution when the Higgs boson decay is loop-induced. We present results for the well-studied $gg \to H \to γγ$ process and for the rare $gg \to H \to Zγ$ mode. In both cases, the interference is destructive, reducing the resonant Higgs boson production rate by about 1.6\% in the diphoton channel and by roughly 3\% in the $Zγ$ decay mode.

AI.tldr: This paper summarizes recent progress in higher-order computations of signal-background interference effects in Higgs boson production via gluon fusion, focusing on the resonance region. For $gg \to H \to \gamma\gamma$ and $gg \to H \to Z\gamma$ processes, interference is destructive, reducing the production rate by ~1.6% and ~3%, respectively.
AI.motivation: To accurately compute signal-background interference effects in Higgs boson production via gluon fusion, particularly in the resonance region where interference terms are most significant relative to the pure signal when the Higgs decay is loop-induced.
AI.method: Higher-order perturbative computations of signal-background interference for $gg \to H \to \gamma\gamma$ and $gg \to H \to Z\gamma$ processes.
AI.result: Destructive interference reduces the resonant Higgs production rate by about 1.6% in the diphoton channel and roughly 3% in the $Z\gamma$ decay mode.
AI.conclusion: Signal-background interference in gluon-fusion Higgs production leads to small but non-negligible destructive corrections in both $\gamma\gamma$ and $Z\gamma$ channels, with the effect being larger in the latter.

title: Novel $\mathcal{N}=2$ higher-spin supercurrents
comment: 0+13 pages; In honor of the 70th anniversary of the Bogoliubov Laboratory of Theoretical Physics
summary: We study cubic interactions of $\mathcal N=2$ massless integer-spin gauge supermultiplets in harmonic superspace. We construct the complete class of abelian $(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{s_1},\mathbf{s_2})$ cubic vertices with the minimal number of space-time derivatives. Such vertices exist only for $\mathbf{s}\geq \mathbf{s_1}+\mathbf{s_2}$ and universally take the form of the gauge prepotential coupled to the conserved higher-spin supercurrent. For~$\mathbf{s_1}\neq\mathbf{s_2}$, we find the novel complex principal supercurrent, whose real and imaginary parts generate the parity-invariant and the parity-breaking interactions, respectively. The supercurrents are constructed from gauge-invariant $\mathcal N=2$ higher-spin Weyl supertensors associated with the spin-$\mathbf{s_1}$ and spin-$\mathbf{s_2}$ gauge multiplets. These supertensors are defined in terms of unconstrained higher-spin analytic prepotentials. We also derive the complete set of conserved component higher-spin currents associated with the $(s,s_1,s_2)$ vertices, including both traceless currents and currents with the non-vanishing trace.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs cubic interactions of N=2 massless integer-spin gauge supermultiplets in harmonic superspace, deriving abelian vertices that universally couple gauge prepotentials to conserved higher-spin supercurrents, with novel complex principal supercurrents for non-equal spins.
AI.motivation: To study and construct cubic interactions of N=2 massless integer-spin gauge supermultiplets in harmonic superspace, specifically focusing on abelian vertices with minimal space-time derivatives.
AI.method: Using harmonic superspace formalism, the authors construct abelian (s,s1,s2) cubic vertices, define gauge-invariant N=2 higher-spin Weyl supertensors from unconstrained analytic prepotentials, and derive conserved component higher-spin currents.
AI.result: Vertices exist only for s ≥ s1+s2; for s1≠s2, a novel complex principal supercurrent emerges whose real and imaginary parts generate parity-invariant and parity-breaking interactions respectively; complete set of conserved component higher-spin currents (traceless and with trace) is derived.
AI.conclusion: The cubic vertices universally take the form of gauge prepotential coupled to conserved higher-spin supercurrent, with supercurrents constructed from N=2 higher-spin Weyl supertensors defined via unconstrained analytic prepotentials.

title: Gravitational Wave Imprints of a High-Quality Axion and the Origin of Flavor Hierarchies
summary: Axions, arising from an anomalous global Peccei-Quinn symmetry $U(1)_{\text{PQ}}$, offer a compelling solution to the strong CP problem but are vulnerable to Planck-suppressed operators. Gauged abelian flavor symmetries $U(1)_F$, invoked to explain the flavor hierarchies via the Froggatt-Nielsen mechanism, can naturally shield the axion from such effects, yielding an accidental high-quality flavored axion with unit domain wall number. Such constructions predict two complementary signatures: (i) flavor-changing neutral currents from $K\toπa$ decays, typically associated with high flavor scales $Λ_{\text{FN}}\gtrsim f_a$, and (ii) stochastic Gravitational Waves (GWs) sourced by the evolution and decay of gauged flavonic and axionic cosmic-string networks. In addition, global axionic strings can efficiently radiate axions, potentially accounting for the observed dark matter relic abundance. We show that the resulting characteristic plateau--valley structure in the GW spectrum provides a distinctive and powerful probe of high-quality flavored axion dark matter models, complementary to low-energy flavor experiments.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes that gauged flavor symmetries can naturally protect axions from Planck-suppressed operators, producing a high-quality flavored axion with unit domain wall number, and predicts complementary signatures: flavor-changing neutral currents (K→πa decays) and gravitational waves from cosmic-string networks, potentially explaining dark matter.
AI.motivation: Axions from Peccei-Quinn symmetry solve the strong CP problem but are vulnerable to Planck-suppressed operators that degrade axion quality; the paper seeks to use gauged flavor symmetries to naturally shield the axion from such effects.
AI.method: The authors construct a theoretical framework where gauged U(1)_F flavor symmetries (Froggatt-Nielsen mechanism) yield an accidental high-quality flavored axion with unit domain wall number, and analyze GW spectra from cosmic-string networks alongside flavor-changing neutral current constraints.
AI.result: The model predicts two complementary signatures: (i) flavor-changing neutral currents from K→πa decays at high flavor scales Λ_FN ≳ f_a, and (ii) stochastic GWs from gauged flavonic and axionic cosmic-string networks. Global axionic string radiation could explain dark matter relic abundance.
AI.conclusion: The characteristic plateau–valley structure in the GW spectrum is a distinctive probe of high-quality flavored axion dark matter models, complementary to low-energy flavor experiments.

title: BPS Non-Renormalization in the BMN Matrix Model
summary: We show in the $(0+1)$-dimensional Berenstein-Maldacena-Nastase matrix model, dual to M-theory on a pp-wave background, that the coupling can be changed between any two finite, non-zero values using a special class of deformations, known as conjugation deformations. Importantly, we prove that they preserve normalizability of the states. This implies that BPS states in the model cannot lift as the couplings are varied, and hence their (unsigned) number cannot change, except at the free point and Banks-Fischler-Shenker-Susskind point.

AI.tldr: In the BMN matrix model (dual to M-theory on a pp-wave background), conjugation deformations allow changing the coupling between any two finite non-zero values while preserving state normalizability, proving BPS states cannot lift and their number remains constant except at free and BFSS points.
AI.motivation: To understand whether BPS states in the BMN matrix model can lift (change in number) as the coupling is varied, which is important for understanding the duality and non-perturbative physics.
AI.method: Use a special class of deformations called conjugation deformations to vary the coupling in the (0+1)-dimensional BMN matrix model, and prove that these deformations preserve normalizability of the states.
AI.result: Conjugation deformations can change the coupling between any two finite, non-zero values. They preserve normalizability, implying BPS states cannot lift as couplings vary, except at the free coupling point and the BFSS point.
AI.conclusion: The (unsigned) number of BPS states remains invariant under coupling variations in the BMN matrix model, with only two exceptional points (free point and BFSS point) where this may not hold.

title: Muon-induced di-tau production as a probe of new physics
summary: The muon trident process, which involves coherent scattering to produce tau pairs, is a powerful tool for constraining dark sectors. We propose to explore this channel using future high-energy muon beams with the dedicated active-target detector, High-Energy Muon Electronic Research Apparatus (HEMERA). The detector would complement muon beam-dump searches by resolving prompt signatures and could operate from preparatory facilities involving an individual muon beam to the full Muon Collider. We illustrate its capabilities for a leptophilic scalar with Yukawa-like couplings that can mediate thermal dark matter production. With $10^{18}$ incident TeV-scale muons, even a compact 10 kg silicon-based HEMERA will extend current $B$-factory and $(g-2)_μ$ bounds by over an order of magnitude in coupling strength, providing an additional compelling motivation for the development of high-energy muon beam infrastructure.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes using a dedicated active-target detector (HEMERA) with future high-energy muon beams to study muon trident production of tau pairs, which can constrain dark sectors. With 10^18 TeV-scale muons, a compact 10 kg silicon detector can improve current bounds on leptophilic scalar couplings by over an order of magnitude.
AI.motivation: The muon trident process (coherent scattering producing tau pairs) offers a powerful way to constrain dark sectors. Current bounds from B-factories and (g-2)_μ leave room for new physics, and high-energy muon beams provide a unique opportunity to probe these couplings more precisely.
AI.method: The authors propose HEMERA, a compact 10 kg silicon-based active-target detector, to be used with future high-energy muon beams (from preparatory facilities to a full Muon Collider). They analyze its capability to detect prompt signatures from muon trident production of tau pairs, specifically for a leptophilic scalar mediator with Yukawa-like couplings relevant to thermal dark matter.
AI.result: With 10^18 incident TeV-scale muons, HEMERA can extend current B-factory and (g-2)_μ bounds on the coupling strength by over an order of magnitude.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach provides compelling additional motivation for developing high-energy muon beam infrastructure, as it significantly enhances sensitivity to dark sectors beyond existing constraints.

title: Carrollian holography with agentic AI: Real mass is imaginary
summary: We introduce LACIA, a verification-driven agentic AI workflow for theoretical physics, and apply it with independent human checks to construct Carrollian conformal bases. We develop the Poincare-Carrollian intertwiner as the central method. It reproduces the celestial and Carrollian conformal bases for massless particles and constructs the missing Carrollian bases for massive and tachyonic particles. The massive basis requires a complex momentum shift in scattering amplitudes.

AI.tldr: LACIA is a verification-driven AI workflow applied to theoretical physics that uses a Poincare-Carrollian intertwiner to construct conformal bases for massive and tachyonic particles, complementing existing massless bases.
AI.motivation: To construct Carrollian conformal bases for massive and tachyonic particles, which were previously missing, using a verification-driven AI approach.
AI.method: Develops a Poincare-Carrollian intertwiner as the central method, applied via the LACIA verification-driven agentic AI workflow with independent human checks.
AI.result: Reproduces existing celestial and Carrollian conformal bases for massless particles, and constructs new Carrollian bases for massive and tachyonic particles. The massive basis requires a complex momentum shift in scattering amplitudes.
AI.conclusion: LACIA successfully constructs complete Carrollian conformal bases across all particle types (massless, massive, tachyonic), demonstrating the utility of verification-driven AI in theoretical physics.

title: BSMArt 2: simpler and faster parameter space scans
comment: 72 pages, including code listings and figures
summary: We present version 2 of BSMArt, a powerful yet lightweight scanning tool designed to simplify the exploration of parameter spaces of new physics models. Aside from architectural improvements, simpler installation and expanded documentation with examples, the new version includes additional tools and new machine learning and Monte Carlo scanning algorithms: Affine MC, Contour Finding, MLScanner, DLScanner, MLS, and CMA-ES. We showcase two variants of CMA-ES scans with physics applications relevant for soft lepton excesses at the LHC. We demonstrate that it is easily possible to find diverse and interesting parameter points for future testing.

AI.tldr: BSMArt version 2 is an upgraded scanning tool for exploring new physics parameter spaces, featuring new ML and Monte Carlo algorithms (Affine MC, Contour Finding, MLScanner, DLScanner, MLS, CMA-ES), with CMA-ES demonstrated for soft lepton excesses at the LHC.
AI.motivation: To simplify and accelerate the exploration of parameter spaces in beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) physics models, enabling efficient discovery of diverse and interesting parameter points.
AI.method: BSMArt v2 introduces architectural improvements, simpler installation, expanded documentation, and integrates new scanning algorithms including Affine MC, Contour Finding, MLScanner, DLScanner, MLS, and CMA-ES.
AI.result: CMA-ES scans successfully identify diverse and interesting parameter points relevant to soft lepton excesses at the LHC.
AI.conclusion: BSMArt v2 provides a lightweight yet powerful tool for efficiently scanning BSM physics parameter spaces, with demonstrated utility for LHC anomaly interpretation.

title: Optical properties of gravitating strings
summary: We study the optical properties of gravitating Abelian-Higgs cosmic strings and compare them with those of the idealized infinitely thin string. We analyze the structure of the corresponding vortex solutions, characterizing their width, curvature profile, and approach to the ideal string limit. By investigating photon propagation in the string spacetime, we show that the finite core of the vortex gives rise to distinctive observational signatures absent in the ideal string approximation, including a characteristic triple-imaging configuration, strong demagnification of the central image, and a nontrivial Shapiro time delay between external and internal images. We determine how these effects depend on the parameters of the Abelian-Higgs model and show that the sign of the time delay is controlled by the ratio of the gauge boson mass to the Higgs boson mass, causing the string core to behave as either a temporal shortcut or a temporal barrier. Our results demonstrate that lensing effects can reveal information about the vortex formation and internal structure.

AI.tldr: This paper studies optical properties of gravitating Abelian-Higgs cosmic strings, showing that their finite core produces distinctive lensing signatures—triple imaging, central image demagnification, and nontrivial Shapiro time delay—that depend on the gauge-to-Higgs mass ratio and are absent in the idealized infinitely thin string approximation.
AI.motivation: To move beyond the idealized infinitely thin string approximation and understand how the finite core structure of realistic cosmic strings affects their observational signatures, particularly gravitational lensing.
AI.method: The authors analyze vortex solutions of the Abelian-Higgs model, characterizing their width and curvature profile, and investigate photon propagation in the string spacetime to study lensing effects such as image formation and Shapiro time delay.
AI.result: Finite-core strings produce triple-imaging, strong demagnification of the central image, and a Shapiro time delay whose sign is determined by the ratio of gauge boson mass to Higgs boson mass (acting as a temporal shortcut or barrier). Core effects yield distinctive signatures absent for infinitely thin strings.
AI.conclusion: Lensing effects can reveal information about the vortex formation and internal structure of cosmic strings, making them observable probes beyond the ideal string approximation.

title: Diffractive open charm photoproduction in ultraperipheral lead-lead and proton-lead collisions at the LHC
summary: We calculate diffractive $D^{0}$ photoproduction in ultraperipheral lead--lead (Pb--Pb) collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) within the recently developed G$γ$A--FONLL framework, where photon--lead diffraction is modeled using nuclear diffractive parton distributions obtained in the leading twist shadowing approach and the photon fluxes include corrections for independent electromagnetic dissociation accompanying the hard photoproduction process. We then use the predicted diffractive cross section to quantify the coherent diffractive contribution rejected by the $Xn0n$ neutron-tagged event selection adopted in the first measurement of $D^0$ photoproduction in Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC, which requires neutron emission from only one of the two lead nuclei. In this work, we also extend the G$γ$A--FONLL framework to proton--lead ($p$--Pb) UPCs and present predictions for inclusive and diffractive $D^{0}$ photoproduction at the LHC. In this case, the dominant configuration is photon emission from the lead ion followed by photon--proton scattering, and the diffractive contribution is evaluated using proton diffractive parton distributions constrained by HERA data.

AI.tldr: The paper calculates diffractive D⁰ photoproduction in ultraperipheral Pb–Pb and p–Pb collisions at the LHC using the GγA–FONLL framework, modeling nuclear diffractive parton distributions via leading twist shadowing and including electromagnetic dissociation corrections. It quantifies the coherent diffractive contribution excluded by neutron-tagged event selection in existing LHC measurements, and extends predictions to p–Pb UPCs using proton diffractive parton distributions from HERA.
AI.motivation: To quantify the coherent diffractive contribution that is rejected by the Xn0n neutron-tagged event selection used in the first LHC measurement of D⁰ photoproduction in Pb–Pb collisions, and to extend the GγA–FONLL framework to p–Pb UPCs for inclusive and diffractive predictions.
AI.method: The GγA–FONLL framework is employed: photon–lead diffraction uses nuclear diffractive parton distributions from the leading twist shadowing approach; photon fluxes include corrections for independent electromagnetic dissociation. For p–Pb, photon emission from lead followed by photon–proton scattering is modeled with proton diffractive parton distributions from HERA.
AI.result: Predictions for diffractive D⁰ photoproduction cross sections in both Pb–Pb and p–Pb UPCs at the LHC, including quantification of the coherent diffractive contribution rejected by Xn0n neutron-tagged event selection.
AI.conclusion: The GγA–FONLL framework successfully models diffractive D⁰ photoproduction in heavy-ion UPCs and provides predictions for future LHC measurements, with the coherent diffractive component being separable via event selection criteria.

title: The spectrum of the bosonic ambitwistor string revisited
summary: We revisit the calculation of the spectrum of the bosonic ambitwistor string, understood as the BRST cohomology or, equivalently, as the semi-infinite cohomology of the $\mathrm{BMS}_3$ Lie algebra relative to the centre with values in a particular module. We work in momentum space, which allows us to work algebraically and interpret the BRST cohomology as inducing representations of the Poincaré group. In agreement with the existing literature, we find that all the cohomology resides in the massless sector, but a careful representation-theoretic analysis of the spectrum reveals, in addition to the usual massless sector of the closed bosonic string (dilaton, metric and Kalb--Ramond field), also a massless vector. We devote a large part of the paper to describing the cohomology at a massless momentum $p$ as a module over the stabiliser $H$ of $p$ in the Lorentz group, a task which is made difficult due to $H$ not acting reducibly when $p\neq 0$. This allows us to conclude that the spectrum is not unitary, forbidding the interpretation of the extra massless vector as a Maxwell field.

AI.tldr: This paper revisits the bosonic ambitwistor string spectrum via BRST cohomology of the BMS₃ Lie algebra, finding that while all cohomology is massless, an extra massless vector appears alongside the usual dilaton, metric, and Kalb-Ramond field. A detailed representation-theoretic analysis shows this vector is non-unitary, precluding it from being a Maxwell field.
AI.motivation: To carefully analyze the spectrum of the bosonic ambitwistor string using BRST cohomology and representation theory, particularly to understand the precise particle content and unitarity properties beyond what was previously reported.
AI.method: The authors compute the BRST cohomology (semi-infinite cohomology of the BMS₃ Lie algebra relative to the centre) in momentum space, treating it algebraically to induce representations of the Poincaré group. They analyze the cohomology at massless momentum p as a module over the stabiliser H of p in the Lorentz group, handling the complexity of H not acting reducibly when p≠0.
AI.result: All cohomology is massless. The spectrum contains the usual massless sector (dilaton, metric, Kalb-Ramond field) plus an additional massless vector. However, the spectrum is non-unitary, preventing the extra vector from being interpreted as a Maxwell field.
AI.conclusion: The bosonic ambitwistor string spectrum is non-unitary, ruling out the extra massless vector as a physical Maxwell field, which has implications for the consistency of the ambitwistor string as a physical theory.

title: Pion structure in Holographic QCD
summary: We employ a holographic model with a modified background that incorporates effective descriptions of key QCD features, including linear confinement and gluon condensation, to study the pion's internal structure, encompassing its mass spectrum as well as electromagnetic and gravitational form factors. This model is capable of simultaneously describing these diverse observables and reaches reasonable agreement with both experimental measurements and lattice QCD results. Our findings indicate that the model captures essential aspects of the pion. The description of multiple structure observables supports its potential as a useful tool for further investigations of pion properties.

AI.tldr: A holographic QCD model with modified background (linear confinement + gluon condensation) simultaneously describes pion mass spectrum, electromagnetic and gravitational form factors, matching experimental and lattice QCD data.
AI.motivation: To develop a holographic model that can simultaneously describe multiple pion observables (mass spectrum, electromagnetic and gravitational form factors) within a single framework, bridging QCD theory and experimental/lattice results.
AI.method: Using a holographic model with a modified background that incorporates effective descriptions of linear confinement and gluon condensation to study the pion's internal structure.
AI.result: The model simultaneously describes the pion's mass spectrum, electromagnetic and gravitational form factors, reaching reasonable agreement with both experimental measurements and lattice QCD results.
AI.conclusion: The model captures essential aspects of the pion, and its ability to describe multiple structure observables supports its potential as a useful tool for further investigations of pion properties.

title: Dirichlet walls and the end of time
summary: We study evolution in Einstein-Hilbert gravity with Dirichlet boundary conditions imposed on a finite surface. We argue that there are open sets of initial data where such evolutions terminate at finite times due to singularities that reach the boundary. In any dimension, the simplest such examples occur in cosmologies. However, in 2+1 dimensions we also show that Dirichlet walls initially outside a BTZ black hole can fall through the horizon, and that this also leads to generic singularities. A similar construction in higher dimensions leads to trapped surfaces that reach the wall, though the end result of such evolutions is more difficult to study.

AI.tldr: This paper studies Einstein-Hilbert gravity with Dirichlet boundary conditions on a finite surface, finding that evolutions can terminate at finite times due to singularities reaching the boundary in cosmologies and in black hole contexts (e.g., BTZ in 2+1D, trapped surfaces in higher dimensions).
AI.motivation: To investigate the dynamical behavior and potential finite-time termination of gravitational evolutions when Dirichlet boundary conditions are imposed on a finite surface, beyond the usual asymptotic boundary conditions.
AI.method: Analytical study of Einstein-Hilbert gravity with Dirichlet boundary conditions on a finite surface, analyzing initial data sets in cosmologies and black hole spacetimes (BTZ in 2+1D, higher-dimensional analogs).
AI.result: Open sets of initial data lead to finite-time evolution termination due to boundary-reaching singularities. In 2+1D, Dirichlet walls outside a BTZ black hole can fall through the horizon, generically producing singularities. In higher dimensions, trapped surfaces reaching the wall arise, though the final state is harder to analyze.
AI.conclusion: Dirichlet boundary conditions on a finite surface in Einstein-Hilbert gravity generically lead to singularities that terminate evolution in finite time, both in cosmological and black hole settings across dimensions.

title: QCD Sum Rule Analysis of a Compact $D^{+}D^{-}K^{+}$-Like Hidden-Charm Hexaquark with $J^{P}=0^{-}$
summary: In this work, we study a compact hexaquark configuration motivated by the same quark content as $D^{+} D^{-} K^+$ using QCD sum rules, where the $D D K$ system has been extensively studied within theoretical frameworks of few-body hadronic dynamics and coupled-channel interactions. The state is constructed from three color-octet quark--antiquark clusters coupled to an overall color singlet. We construct six independent local interpolating currents with the quantum numbers $J^{P}=0^{-}$ and analyze the corresponding two-point correlation functions. Both perturbative contributions and nonperturbative condensates up to dimension ten are included in the operator product expansion. Our analysis indicates that, within Borel windows satisfying standard sum rule criteria and with a reasonable choice of continuum threshold, the mass of the $J^{P}=0^{-}$ hidden-charm hexaquark state is estimated to be in the range $3.94$--$4.41~\mathrm{GeV}$. This prediction can provide a valuable theoretical reference for identifying such exotic hidden-charm hexaquark state in future experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper uses QCD sum rules to study a compact hexaquark state (with the same quark content as $D^{+}D^{-}K^+$) and predicts its mass to be in the range 3.94--4.41 GeV for $J^{P}=0^{-}$.
AI.motivation: To study a compact hexaquark configuration motivated by the $D D K$ system, which has been extensively studied in few-body hadronic dynamics and coupled-channel interactions, and to provide a theoretical reference for identifying such exotic hidden-charm hexaquark states in experiments.
AI.method: The authors construct six independent local interpolating currents with $J^{P}=0^{-}$ using three color-octet quark-antiquark clusters coupled to an overall color singlet. They analyze two-point correlation functions using QCD sum rules, including perturbative contributions and nonperturbative condensates up to dimension ten in the operator product expansion.
AI.result: Within Borel windows satisfying standard sum rule criteria and with a reasonable continuum threshold, the mass of the $J^{P}=0^{-}$ hidden-charm hexaquark state is estimated to be 3.94--4.41 GeV.
AI.conclusion: The predicted mass range provides a valuable theoretical reference for identifying such exotic hidden-charm hexaquark states in future experiments.

title: Hodge theory and $G_4$ fluxes in weighted projective spaces: Galois action
summary:
We extend the explicit study of $G_4$-fluxes and general Hodge cycles from the ordinary Fermat sextic fourfold to tame Fermat-type hypersurfaces in weighted projective space. The main new feature in the weighted setting is that the Galois action on the cyclotomic period data need not preserve the $(2,2)$-subspace. As a consequence, the rational reconstruction of an integral self-dual class can involve additional middle-cohomology components, increasing the norm of the corresponding flux.
  We work at maximally symmetric Fermat points, where the period matrices and symmetry-invariant Hodge loci can be computed explicitly. Using Movasati's description of periods, cyclotomic period matrices, and Hermite/Smith normal form reductions, we construct the relevant integral lattices of symmetric self-dual classes in middle cohomology. This gives a controlled test of whether symmetric general Hodge cycles can satisfy the M2-brane tadpole bound.
  Our main conclusion is empirical. In the degree 12 example in $\mathbb{P}_{1,1,1,1,4,4}$, and in the degree 8 weighted example used as a comparison, the shortest computed symmetric general Hodge cycles overshoot the tadpole bound. In the degree 36 example in $\mathbb{P}_{1,1,1,9,12,12}$, which has $h^{1,1}=11$, the most general example we have, the tadpole conjecture is indeed verified at the maximally symmetric locus, although the computations get difficult and computationally expensive.
  These computations suggest that, in weighted Fermat examples, the relevant notion of a ``symmetric flux'' must take into account not only automorphisms of the variety but also the Galois action on the period field. Non-uniform Galois orbits provide a natural arithmetic mechanism by which symmetric Hodge classes can acquire large tadpole charge.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the study of G₄-fluxes and general Hodge cycles from Fermat sextic fourfolds to weighted Fermat-type hypersurfaces. The key finding is that symmetric general Hodge cycles in these weighted settings tend to overshoot the M2-brane tadpole bound, suggesting that Galois action on period fields must be considered as an arithmetic mechanism contributing to large tadpole charge.
AI.motivation: To understand whether symmetric general Hodge cycles (fluxes) in weighted Fermat-type hypersurfaces can satisfy the M2-brane tadpole bound, extending previous work on ordinary Fermat sextic fourfolds to more general weighted projective spaces.
AI.method: The authors work at maximally symmetric Fermat points, compute period matrices and symmetry-invariant Hodge loci explicitly using Movasati's description of periods, cyclotomic period matrices, and Hermite/Smith normal form reductions to construct integral lattices of symmetric self-dual classes in middle cohomology.
AI.result: In all tested weighted examples (degree 12 in ℙ₁,₁,₁,₁,₄,₄, degree 8 weighted comparison, and degree 36 in ℙ₁,₁,₁,₉,₁₂,₁₂), the shortest computed symmetric general Hodge cycles overshoot the tadpole bound. The degree 36 example (h¹·¹=11) verifies the tadpole conjecture at the maximally symmetric locus.
AI.conclusion: In weighted Fermat examples, symmetric flux must account for both automorphisms of the variety and Galois action on the period field. Non-uniform Galois orbits provide an arithmetic mechanism for symmetric Hodge classes to acquire large tadpole charge.

title: Probing Quantum Numbers and Decay Branching Ratios of Exotic States via Entanglement-Enabled Spin Interference
summary: Ultra-peripheral heavy-ion collisions (UPCs) coherently photo-produce vector mesons through two spatially separated and quantum-mechanically indistinguishable production sites, whose separation far exceeds the lifetime of the created resonance. The superposition of these amplitudes generates production-site entanglement, observed experimentally as entanglement-enabled spin-interference patterns in the angular distributions of the decay products. We show that these interference signatures provide a sensitive probe of spin-alignment transfer in hadronic decay chains, enabling intermediate-state quantum numbers and relative branching ratios to be measured from observed angular modulations. Using the decay $ρ(1450)\!\rightarrow\!π^{+}π^{-}π^{+}π^{-}$ as example, we simulate the $a_{1}(1260)π$, $h_{1}(1170)π$, $ρ(ππ)_{S}$, and $π(1300)π$ channels and demonstrate that each produces a distinct azimuthal $\cos 2φ$ modulation. The $π(1300)π$ mode shows a uniquely separated response, allowing its branching fraction to be extracted directly. These results establish production-site entanglement in UPCs as a selective tool for hadron spectroscopy, particularly for broad or overlapping resonances that are otherwise difficult to disentangle.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that entanglement from two spatially separated production sites in ultra-peripheral heavy-ion collisions (UPCs) creates spin-interference patterns in vector meson decays, which can be used to measure intermediate-state quantum numbers and branching ratios, demonstrated via the $\rho(1450) \to 4\pi$ decay.
AI.motivation: To develop a selective tool for hadron spectroscopy that can disentangle broad or overlapping resonances, which are difficult to study using conventional methods.
AI.method: The authors analyze production-site entanglement in UPCs, where two indistinguishable production sites (separated beyond the resonance lifetime) create spin-interference patterns. They simulate the $\rho(1450) \to 4\pi$ decay through four channels ($a_1(1260)\pi$, $h_1(1170)\pi$, $\rho(\pi\pi)_S$, and $\pi(1300)\pi$) and compute the resulting azimuthal $\cos 2\phi$ modulation signatures.
AI.result: Each decay channel produces a distinct $\cos 2\phi$ modulation pattern, with the $\pi(1300)\pi$ mode showing a uniquely separated response that allows direct extraction of its branching fraction.
AI.conclusion: Production-site entanglement in UPCs serves as a selective tool for hadron spectroscopy, particularly effective for disentangling broad or overlapping resonances.

title: Notes on (-2)-form symmetries
summary: We study $(-2)$-form symmetries of a $d$-dimensional quantum field theory, via a $(-1)$-form symmetry of its $(d+1)$-dimensional Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT), realized by a non-genuine codimension-one defect in the SymTFT bulk attached to a spacetime-filling topological operator. Unlike a $(-1)$-form symmetry of a $d$-dimensional theory, which merely shifts a parameter of the absolute theory, a $(-2)$-form symmetry modifies the SymTFT action, and thereby relates theories whose ordinary global symmetries differ by anomaly data or by the associator data of a non-invertible symmetry. We illustrate the construction in two-dimensional toy models, three-dimensional ABJM-type theories, four-dimensional generalized Yang--Mills theory, and in a fusion-categorical example relating the non-invertible symmetries $\operatorname{Rep}(D_4)$ and $\operatorname{Rep}(Q_8)$. We then develop a club-sandwich realization, in which a quarter-gauging operation interfaces between IR phases of distinct RG flows of a common UV theory, and an alternative realization via nested discrete gauging. Finally, we present a holographic, top-down realization in which the type IIA Romans mass plays the role of a $(-2)$-form background for a three-dimensional Chern--Simons-matter theory, with shifts of the Romans mass realizing shifts of the boundary anomaly coefficients. We also discuss related constructions for coupled bulk--boundary systems.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces $(-2)$-form symmetries in QFT via a SymTFT framework, showing they modify the SymTFT action and relate theories with different anomaly or associator data, with applications to toy models, ABJM, Yang-Mills, fusion categories, and a holographic realization using Romans mass in type IIA string theory.
AI.motivation: To extend the notion of higher-form symmetries to $(-2)$-form symmetries, which provide a new organizational principle for relating quantum field theories that differ in their global symmetry structure, anomaly data, or non-invertible symmetry associators, beyond what $(-1)$-form symmetries can capture.
AI.method: The authors construct $(-2)$-form symmetries using a $(-1)$-form symmetry in the $(d+1)$-dimensional SymTFT bulk, realized by a non-genuine codimension-one defect attached to a spacetime-filling operator. They develop a club-sandwich realization via quarter-gauging, an alternative via nested discrete gauging, and a top-down holographic realization where the type IIA Romans mass is a $(-2)$-form background.
AI.result: The $(-2)$-form symmetry modifies the SymTFT action, relating theories whose ordinary symmetries differ by anomaly data or associator data of non-invertible symmetries. Concrete examples include two-dimensional toy models, 3d ABJM-type theories, 4d generalized Yang-Mills, and the fusion-categorical relation between Rep(D_4) and Rep(Q_8).
AI.conclusion: $(-2)$-form symmetries offer a systematic way to connect QFTs with distinct global symmetry data via SymTFT, with both field-theoretic and holographic realizations, and may generalize to $(-k)$-form symmetries in higher dimensions for coupled bulk-boundary systems.

title: Pion transitions in the Born-Oppenheimer Effective Field Theory: a long distance approach
summary: We address pion transitions involving heavy quarkonium and heavy exotic states in the Born-Oppenheimer effective field theory. Many of these states have a size similar or larger than the typical hadronic scale, and hence the usual QCD multipole expansion breaks down. Unknown low energy functions must be introduced, which at short distances must reproduce the known results of the multipole expansion. In order to determine the long distance behavior of these functions, we propose an interaction Lagrangian for pions and the QCD string. By matching the amplitudes obtained with this Lagrangian to the ones of the Born-Oppenheimer effective field theory in the static limit, we obtain the low energy functions in terms of three universal parameters. As a by product, we also obtain the light quark mass dependence of the string tension. Assuming that the low energy functions are long-distance dominated, we calculate several quarkonium-to-quarkonium and hybrid-to-quarkonium transitions. We estimate the universal constants and provide a phenomenological analysis of the most relevant transitions.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a Born-Oppenheimer effective field theory framework to describe pion transitions involving heavy quarkonium and exotic states, introducing an interaction Lagrangian for pions and the QCD string to determine low-energy functions and calculate various hadronic transitions.
AI.motivation: Standard QCD multipole expansion fails for heavy quarkonium and exotic states whose size is comparable to or larger than the typical hadronic scale. The authors aim to develop a more general framework to describe pion transitions in these systems.
AI.method: The authors propose an interaction Lagrangian for pions and the QCD string, matching amplitudes to the Born-Oppenheimer effective field theory in the static limit. This yields low-energy functions expressed in terms of three universal parameters. They also derive the light quark mass dependence of the string tension.
AI.result: The low-energy functions are obtained in terms of three universal parameters. Assuming these functions are long-distance dominated, the authors calculate various quarkonium-to-quarkonium and hybrid-to-quarkonium transitions, estimate the universal constants, and provide a phenomenological analysis.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework extends beyond the limitations of the QCD multipole expansion, enabling description of pion transitions for heavy hadronic states of arbitrary size, with phenomenological predictions for relevant transitions.

title: Charting the different phases of Yang-Mills-Chern-Simons-Higgs theories
summary: We explore Yang-Mills-Chern-Simons theories coupled to a Higgs-like field in the fundamental representation of $SU(2)$ quantized in linear covariant gauges in three Euclidean dimensions. We analyze the modifications in the analytic structure of the gluon propagator due to the elimination of infinitesimal Gribov copies. The interplay between the Higgs, the Chern-Simons and Gribov mass parameters is investigated. Two different phases are identified: a confining one, where all poles are complex, and a deconfined one, where would-be physical gluon excitation can appear. Unlike previous works, the Gribov parameter is consistently fixed by its gap equation as a function of the other mass parameters and the gauge coupling. This imposes a constraint in the parameter space and makes transparent how the competition of the mass parameters affects the relevance of the Gribov parameter for the characterization of the spectrum of the theory.

title: Search for heavy Majorana neutrinos at muon-proton colliders via lepton-number-violating signals
summary: We propose a novel search strategy for heavy Majorana neutrinos based on the lepton-number-violating process $μ^{-}p \to jN \to j(\ell^{+}W^{-})$ at future muon-proton ($μp$) colliders equipped with 1 TeV muon beams and 7 TeV proton beams, yielding a center-of-mass energy of approximately 5.3 TeV. For heavy neutrinos with masses in the range $200~\text{GeV} \lesssim m_N \lesssim 1000~\text{GeV}$, this analysis targets the decay chain $N \to \ell^{+}W^{-} \to \ell^{+}jj$, producing a characteristic final state consisting of one charged lepton and three well-resolved jets. For TeV-scale Majorana neutrinos, the $W$ boson is highly boosted, such that its hadronic decay products coalesce into a prominent fat-jet ($J$) signature. We conduct comprehensive signal and background analyses that account for realistic detector effects to assess the search sensitivity. We derive the projected $2σ$ exclusion limits on the neutrino mixing parameter $|V_{\ell N}|^2$ based on two typical integrated luminosity scenarios of $100~\text{fb}^{-1}$ and $1~\text{ab}^{-1}$. The results demonstrate that the proposed search strategy can achieve constraints substantially superior to the existing bounds from the LHC and other high-energy colliders. This study demonstrates that future $μp$ colliders can provide competitive sensitivity for probing heavy Majorana neutrinos over the mass range $200~\text{GeV} \leq m_N \leq 3000~\text{GeV}$.

Targeting heavy neutrino masses from 200 GeV to 3 TeV, the analysis focuses on the decay chain N → ℓ⁺W⁻ → ℓ⁺jj, yielding a charged lepton plus three jets (or a fat-jet for boosted W bosons). With 1 TeV muon and 7 TeV proton beams (√s ≈ 5.3 TeV), they derive projected 2σ exclusion limits on |V_ℓN|² for 100 fb⁻¹ and 1 ab⁻¹, finding significantly better sensitivity than existing LHC constraints.

title: On Quantum Aspects of 1-Form Symmetries I: BV-BRST Cohomology and Anomaly Polynomials
summary: We investigate the quantum aspects of gauging continuous 1-form global symmetries. In this paper, we study the BV-BRST quantization of a $U(1)$ 2-form gauge field, described geometrically by a $U(1)$ gerbe. Starting from the local Čech data of the gerbe, we construct the corresponding infinitesimal symmetry structure in terms of a Lie 2-algebroid, and show that, together with the associated exact Courant algebroid, it provides a natural geometric framework for the BV-BRST complex of this higher-form gauge theory. In this formulation, the field-ghost tower is encoded directly in the local gerbe data, and the higher Russian formula arises naturally from the relations among the connective structure, the curving, and the 3-form curvature. We further show that the resulting Čech-de Rham bicomplex provides a natural setting for anomaly descent for $U(1)$ 1-form symmetries, and illustrate the construction with explicit examples in Maxwell theory.
